content: Anyone who's here and mentioned in the article want to add clarification/context to their quoted statements? I appreciate that a journalist might even accidentally put a dramatic spin on things
I think my name appears in relation to #general > The role of AI companies in large formalisation projects @ 💬. I’ve been told this message circulated a lot on the largest nazi website.
I have no idea what you think the largest nazi website is.

My guess is that Patrick means the one with a single-letter name, later in the alphabet.
But yes,

Patrick Massot, a mathematician at the Laboratoire de Mathématiques d’Orsay in France, compared the company’s scoop to an “atomic bomb” that would make projects radioactive to young mathematicians, even if that meant missing out on valuable training or the opportunity to develop new ideas.

But I mean people who appeared with what could be editorial spin on things they did or said in response. The article is rather dramatic with people rushing here and there in the real world and having dramatic conversations in response to the news.
4 messages were moved here from #general > Lean in the wild by Johan Commelin.
I think it's unprofessional to call X a nazi website.

Tangent: I agree with the assessment that discourse on X is dominated by right-wing people and bots (and describing its owner's political views as fascist is a justified value judgement). If you like to discuss with actual humans, that's difficult on X (and you may be wasting your time).

@Johan Commelin thanks for the move, and I would I not presume to say my guess is what Patrick meant, merely that I don't know of any other realistic option that might be so described even if one doesn't agree with that description. Apologies for having raised the name. I shall say no more and hope people only talk about the article, to the extent that's possible.

I know quite a lot of left-leaning people who are still using Twitter because that's where their social bubble hangs out and because they've gotten used to the UI (e.g. lots of digital artists), so I wouldn't refer to it as "the largest nazi website" myself because of the implication that carries regardless of the politics of who owns it or what kind of posts are tolerated on the platform :-)

David Michael Roberts said:

Anyone who's here and mentioned in the article want to add clarification/context to their quoted statements? I appreciate that a journalist might even accidentally put a dramatic spin on things

My sympathies are entirely on the side of Sidharth Hariharan, but like David, I also wonder about some of the quotes, particularly this one:

Dr. Han said that those were miscommunications, but that the “fear and Ludditivism” in response had “hardened my resolve” to use A.I. to “formalize all of mathematics.”

When a journalist strings together three separate quoted phrases to make a sentence, I have to wonder how accurately the sentence reflects the original intent. Again, I'm not defending the behavior of Math, Inc., but I wonder if the article goes too far in "demonizing" them. The quote makes Han sound completely unsympathetic to the concerns of mathematicians, whom he calls Luddites. I wonder if that is accurate.

FYI there's a blogpost where Sidharth describes the meeting with Jesse Han
https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/posts/SpherePacking-1/
